evidence.positive: Against the running main build (demo-demo tenant): created a patient via POST /api/admin/patients/, created an ERAS case (p-hysterectomy, eras_operation=t confirmed in DB) started 2h earlier, inserted two BOLUS ondansetron administrations (m-ondansetron-iv + m-ondansetron-oral, both ANTIEMETIC_5HT3_ANTAGONIST) as medication_orders/medication_administrations rows, evicted the Redis patients/demo-demo/<pmrn> cache, then fired POST /api/admin/events/category-event with ERAS_OPERATION_END (case 64070). a-eras-antiemetics fired; the persisted rule_fired_results.prompt.description reads 'Patient has received Ondansetron and Ondansetron, but all administered antiemetics are of class 5HT3-Antagonist. At least two antiemetics...'. The same text came back through the user-facing GET /api/patient/{pmrn}/alert/{resultId} as loopuser (status 200). Repeated with dexamethasone + methylprednisolone (case 86503): prompt reads '...MethylPREDNIsolone and Dexamethasone, but all administered antiemetics are of class Steroid.'
evidence.negative: Same staging with ondansetron IV + dexamethasone (two different classes, case 79642): a-eras-antiemetics did not fire; rule_not_fired_results holds explanation 'Patient received valid antiemetics' and no rule_fired_results row exists. Also, in every fired prompt on the shipped build the raw constant is absent: regex /of class ANTIEMETIC_/ against the full user alert payload for case 64070 returned false, and SQL position('ANTIEMETIC_5HT3' in prompt->>'description') > 0 returned f for case 08995. docker logs for the whole container lifetime contain exactly one 'of class ANTIEMETIC_' line, the one from the red check below.
evidence.red_check: Compiled the parent commit's (cf05a056e) ERASAntiemeticsRule.java inside the app container with javac against /app/classes:/app/libs/* (lombok @Slf4j removed; an explicit slf4j logger added that logs the prompt text as 'PREFIX ERAS antiemetics prompt text: ...' so the gate has a log line to grep). Backed up the shipped ERASAntiemeticsRule.class (sha256 f3a75a94...) and ERASAntiemeticsRule$MedRoutePair.class (cdfec49f...), copied the pre-fix classes over them, docker restart, readiness UP. Re-ran the two-ondansetron scenario on a fresh case (10732): the fired prompt read '...all administered antiemetics are of class ANTIEMETIC_5HT3_ANTAGONIST.' in both rule_fired_results.prompt and the app log at 15:19:47Z. RED. Restored both backed-up classes, confirmed sha256 match (f3a75a94.../cdfec49f...), docker restart (StartedAt 15:20:13Z), re-ran on fresh case 08995: prompt reads 'of class 5HT3-Antagonist' again and the signature line never reappeared after the restart. Data flip is not applicable: the label map is code, not data.

red_check_signature: all administered antiemetics are of class ANTIEMETIC_5HT3_ANTAGONIST
caveats: NK1-Antagonist, Anticholinergic, Sympathomimetic and Antidopaminergic labels were not exercised at runtime; only 5HT3-Antagonist and Steroid were. demo-demo has no NK1 medication (only mayo-mayo has one, and that tenant is disabled here). The map is a single Map.of literal and MasterMedicationListAntiemeticClassTest asserts every master-list antiemetic class is a key of it.

Administrations were staged by SQL insert (demo med-admin user endpoint rolls back on the EMR writer) and the event was fired via the admin category-event endpoint rather than a real procedure-finish; the rule code path from event to prompt is the production one.
The pre-fix class used for the red check had one log statement added so its prompt text reached the application log; the prompt text itself is otherwise never logged.
The prompt was observed via the persisted rule result and the user alert API, not rendered in a browser.

automation.assessment: Unit coverage already satisfies the ticket's ACs: ERASAntiemeticsRuleTest asserts the full prompt with 'of class Steroid', and MasterMedicationListAntiemeticClassTest asserts every antiemetic class in every tenant master list has exactly one key in ANTIEMETIC_CLASS_LABELS. qa-suite has no ERAS antiemetics coverage at all (no spec references a-eras-antiemetics or 'ERAS Protocol'). Worth locking in end to end is the API-level pair below, following the browser-free fired-evaluations pattern; a unit test for the one label not pinned anywhere (NK1-Antagonist) is cheap.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: An ERAS case given two ondansetron doses produced the prompt text "all administered antiemetics are of class 5HT3-Antagonist", and a dexamethasone plus methylprednisolone case produced "of class Steroid", both through the persisted rule result and the user alert API.
Negative: A case given ondansetron plus dexamethasone did not fire the rule, and no fired prompt on the shipped build contained the raw ANTIEMETIC_ constant.
Red check: Swapping in the parent commit's rule class and re-running the two-ondansetron case produced "of class ANTIEMETIC_5HT3_ANTAGONIST"; the shipped class was restored with matching checksums and the readable label returned.

Automation: Unit tests already pin the Steroid label and the label-to-class mapping; proposed an API-level qa-suite pair for the prompt text and a unit case for the NK1-Antagonist label.
